evidence.claim: Two Piedmont peaks protected after a campaign against mineral excavation.
evidence.quote: This led local concerned citizens, educational institutions, and local governments to join together and convince state government pursue the creation of a state park in order to protect the area.

evidence.claim: Two Piedmont peaks
evidence.quote: Crowders Mountain is one of two main peaks within Crowders Mountain State Park, the other peak being The Pinnacle.  The park is located in the Western Piedmont of North Carolina

evidence.claim: Crowders Mountain Drive belongs to North Carolina’s scenic-byway system in the Piedmont.
evidence.quote: PIEDMONT 111 Crowders Mountain Drive 112

evidence.claim: Its namesake rises nearly 800 feet above the surrounding terrain between Kings Mountain and Gastonia.
evidence.quote: The park is located in the Western Piedmont of North Carolina between the cities of Kings Mountain and Gastonia or about 25 miles (40 km) west of Charlotte.  Crowders Mountain abruptly rises nearly 800 feet (240 m) above the surrounding terrain

evidence.claim: Crowders Mountain and The Pinnacle have sheer cliffs 100–150 feet high.
evidence.quote: Both monadnocks present sheer rock cliffs which are 100–150 feet (30–46 m) in height.

evidence.claim: In the early 1970s, mineral exploration prompted citizens, educational institutions and local governments to press for protection.
evidence.quote: In the early 1970s, a mining company began doing exploratory sampling of areas along what is now the Backside Trail with the intent of purchasing the minerals rights to excavate the mountain for kyanite, barite, and iron.

evidence.claim: In the early 1970s, mineral exploration prompted citizens, educational institutions and local governments to press for protection.
evidence.quote: This led local concerned citizens, educational institutions, and local governments to join together and convince state government pursue the creation of a state park in order to protect the area.

evidence.claim: North Carolina created the state park in 1973; Crowders Mountain itself joined it in 1978 and The Pinnacle in 1987.
evidence.quote: In 1973 the State of North Carolina created Crowders Mountain State Park. It opened to the public in 1974. Crowders Mountain proper was added to the new park in 1978. The Pinnacle was added in 1987.

evidence.claim: Kings Mountain lies west of Charlotte along I-85.
evidence.quote: Kings Mountain lies 30 miles (48 km) west of Charlotte along Interstate 85.

evidence.claim: Within the nearby park, Crowders Mountain occupies the northeastern section and The Pinnacle the western section.
evidence.quote: Crowders Mountain, 1,625 feet (495 m), is in the northeastern section of the park.

evidence.claim: The summit views require a hike: trails lead to both peaks, with Charlotte’s towers visible on a clear day.
evidence.quote: Hiking trails lead to both summits, from which it is possible to view the skyscrapers of nearby Charlotte, North Carolina, on a clear day.

evidence.claim: The Pinnacle the western section
evidence.quote: The Pinnacle, 1,705 feet (520 m), is in the western section of the park.

evidence.claim: Kings Mountain took its name from a battlefield across the state line.
evidence.quote: It was decided that "Kings Mountain" would be a more appropriate name since the community was close to the site of the historic 1780 Battle of Kings Mountain in York County, South Carolina

evidence.claim: The settlement had been called White Plains before its incorporation and name change in 1874.
evidence.quote: Originally the settlement was called White Plains, but the city was incorporated on October 16, 1874, and the name was changed.

evidence.claim: Downtown’s local history museum occupies a former post office built in 1940 with Depression-era works funding.
evidence.quote: It is located in the former United States Post Office building, a handsome Colonial Revival structure built in 1940 with funding from a Depression-era works program.

evidence.claim: Postal use ended in 1986. The city acquired the building in 2000 and leased it to the historical society for a museum.
evidence.quote: The building was used as a post office until 1986.  The city acquired the building in 2000 and leased it to the local historical society, which has used it as a museum since.

evidence.claim: Crowders Mountain was once a prospect for mineral excavation.
evidence.quote: with the intent of purchasing the minerals rights to excavate the mountain for kyanite, barite, and iron.

evidence.claim: Exploratory sampling in the early 1970s targeted ground along what is now the Backside Trail.
evidence.quote: In the early 1970s, a mining company began doing exploratory sampling of areas along what is now the Backside Trail

evidence.claim: Local citizens, educational institutions and governments responded by pressing the state to protect the area.
evidence.quote: This led local concerned citizens, educational institutions, and local governments to join together and convince state government pursue the creation of a state park in order to protect the area.

evidence.claim: The mountain became part of the park in 1978.
evidence.quote: Crowders Mountain proper was added to the new park in 1978.

evidence.claim: Its summit also has a separate history of communications: WGNC-FM erected a tower in the late 1940s, and three radio towers occupy a privately owned summit plot.
evidence.quote: One of the first FM radio stations in North Carolina, Gastonia's WGNC-FM, erected a transmission tower on Crowders Mountain in the late 1940s.

evidence.claim: Its summit also has a separate history of communications: WGNC-FM erected a tower in the late 1940s, and three radio towers occupy a privately owned summit plot.
evidence.quote: Today three radio towers are located on the mountain.

evidence.claim: Its summit also has a separate history of communications: WGNC-FM erected a tower in the late 1940s, and three radio towers occupy a privately owned summit plot.
evidence.quote: The transmitters are located within a 12,197-square-foot (1,133.1 m2) plot of land on the summit that remains privately owned.

evidence.claim: At 1,705 feet, The Pinnacle is the highest point in Gaston County.
evidence.quote: The Pinnacle, the highest point in Gaston County at 1,705 feet.

evidence.claim: It is the remnant of a quartzite ridge formed approximately 400–500 million years ago.
evidence.quote: The monadnock is the remnant of a quartzite ridge which formed approximately 400–500 million years ago.

evidence.claim: Softer material that once surrounded and covered it has gradually worn away.
evidence.quote: The softer material that once covered and surrounded the monadnock has been gradually worn down

evidence.claim: The peak belongs to the Kings Mountain Belt, a string of monadnocks and rock types extending through the Carolina Piedmont.
evidence.quote: The Pinnacle is part of the Kings Mountain Belt, a string of monadnocks and rock types along the piedmont in the Carolinas

evidence.claim: A hiking trail reaches the summit, where views can extend west and north to the Blue Ridge and east toward Charlotte.
evidence.quote: A hiking trail leads to the summit, from which it is possible to view the much higher Blue Ridge mountains far to the west and north, and the skyscrapers of Charlotte

evidence.claim: The museum building is Colonial Revival in style. Elsewhere downtown, the Mauney Memorial Library and two historic bridges are among the city’s National Register properties.
evidence.quote: a handsome Colonial Revival structure

evidence.claim: the Mauney Memorial Library and two historic bridges are among the city’s National Register properties
evidence.quote: King Street Overhead Bridge, Margrace Mill Village Historic District, Jacob S. Mauney Memorial Library and Teacher's Home, Southern Railway Company Overhead Bridge, and West End Historic District are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.claim: The towers relay more than commercial radio: wireless phone companies, railroads and local emergency services also use them to carry signals.
evidence.quote: In addition to commercial radio, the towers relay signals for wireless phone companies, railroads and local emergency services.

evidence.claim: Many other formations in the belt can also be seen from the summit, placing this isolated peak within a longer chain.
evidence.quote: many of which can be seen from the summit.

flags: Partial overview: both NCDOT files contain the same truncated guidebook opening, ending before the Crowders route chapter. Only byway inclusion is verifiable; route-specific selection rationale, road character, construction history and end-to-end directions are missing. Kept intro shorter rather than substitute catalog facts.

Dropped unsupported current route claims: Sparrow Springs Road from US 74 east of I-85, Pinnacle Road changing to Lake Montonia Road at the county line, NC 161 endpoint, eight miles and fifteen minutes. The tagline’s circuit around the foot of both peaks is also unverified.
Current mountain and Pinnacle claims have cache support; omitted the true-mountain classification as an unnecessary and poorly substantiated threshold. Preserved approximately for Pinnacle ridge age.

Moment order uses material’s Kings Mountain-to-park order, then northeastern Crowders Mountain to southwestern Pinnacle. Exact driving access order cannot be established from the truncated route cache.
No story-level motifs existed in current; supplied an empty array.
Tribal hunting-boundary and buffalo claims appear only in secondary cache sources; omitted rather than build the story around them.
